pie: suHnús gʰrómom ḱléwt bʰéyh₂t-kʷe. ph₂tḗr prḗḱst kʷíd dyḗws stonh₂éyeti. ph₂tḗr wéwket pérkʷunos h₁ógʷʰim h₂ḱm̥néh₁ gʷʰn̥sḱéti. wédōr h₂ew gʷm̥sḱéti deywós-kʷe h₁ím h₂ew gʷʰn̥sḱéti. mē tréses pós h₂wérst. nu h₂wérst suHnús-kʷe ḱlush₁yét. h₂éǵrōs ǵʰelh₃wṓs h₂éyeri h₁sént. ne bʰéyh₂t swépt-kʷe.
english: A son heard the thunder and was afraid. He asked his father: "Why does the sky thunder?" The father said: "Perkwunos strikes the serpent with the stone. It comes back to the waters, and the god strikes it again. Do not fear: afterwards it rains." Then it rained, and the son listened. In the morning the fields were green. He was not afraid, and he slept.

pie: ph₂tḗr dyḗws ǵʰwḗrm̥ dʰubʰróy mréy kʷéḱt. n̥bʰróns gʷérh₃t dʰǵʰémi-kʷe ne h₂wérst. nu méǵh₂m̥ h₂éḱmonm̥ ní Hyéh₁kt. móri h₁n̥dó séngʷt wódr̥-kʷe yéset. ǵʰwḗrm̥ gʷélh₁t h₁yós h₂én ḱéyo. h₁ésyo krépos dért n̥bʰrṓs-kʷe h₁n̥dʰént. nu h₂wérst srówōs-kʷe pl̥nh₁n̥tó. gʰréh₁mn̥ h₂wékst h₂óweyes-kʷe h₁íd h₁édn̥t. h₂néres h₂éḱmonm̥ pós widónt. h₁ím dʰéh₁si stoh₂éyont h₁ím-kʷe sepelyónt.
english: Father Sky caught sight of the beast in the deep sea. It had swallowed the rain-clouds, and it did not rain on the earth. Then he threw down a great stone. It fell into the sea, and the water boiled. It struck the beast, which lay there in the depths. Its body burst, and the rain-clouds came forth. Then it rained, and the streams became full. The grass grew, and the sheep ate it. Afterwards men found the stone. They set it up in a sacred place and honored it.

pie: dwóh₁ bʰréh₂terh₁e h₁ógʷʰim próti stéygʰetām. h₁óynos bʰéyh₂t h₁éteros dʰérst. h₁yós dʰérst só h₁ím ǵʰoysóh₁ h₁néǵʰt. ǵʰwḗr mért wédōr-kʷe soksṓd h₁éǵʰs h₁éyt. bʰréh₂tēr dṓm drémt h₁yós bʰéyh₂t h₁ludʰíbʰos-kʷe wéwket. bʰréh₂tēr moy ǵʰwḗrm̥ wént h₁ím sepelyéte. h₁éysōm ǵérh₂onts ph₂tḗr mówdoh₁ smḗyt. h₁léwdʰeyes bʰréh₂term̥ sepelyónt h₁ésmey-kʷe déh₃reh₂ kʷékʷlons yugéh₂-kʷe dh₃ént.
english: Two brothers went out against the serpent. The one was afraid; the other took courage. He who took courage stabbed it with a spear. The beast died, and the waters went out from the rock. The brother who had been afraid ran home and said to the people: "My brother slew the beast; praise him!" Their old father laughed with joy. The people honored the brother and gave him gifts: a wheel and a yoke.

pie: h₁suh₁éḱwos h₁éḱwons déh₂newi h₂éǵet. h₂éngʷʰis wédn̥s h₁éǵʰs h₁nédʰt wiHróm-kʷe wih₁tó. h₁éḱwōs h₂epó dr̥h₂ént. wiHrós bʰágom ǵʰuHéyet stúh₂re me spr̥dʰí. bʰágos h₁ím ḱléwt h₂éḱmonm̥-kʷe diwés Hyéh₁kt. kʷŕ̥mim dʰéwgʰt kʷŕ̥mis-kʷe h₁ím léh₁t. h₁suh₁éḱwos bʰéwgt h₁ím-kʷe swóh₁ ǵʰoysóh₁ h₂wégt. h₁ésyo h₁éḱwōs pótim h₂ew h₁ludʰónt. dʰh₁séy déh₃rom lewkóm h₁éḱwom pós déh₃t.
english: Of-Good-Horses drove his horses to the river. A snake came out of the water and wrapped itself around the hero. The horses ran away in fear. The hero called upon the god: "Strong one, free me!" The god heard him and threw a stone from heaven. It hit the worm, and the worm let go of him. Of-Good-Horses got free and pierced it with his spear. His horses came back to their master. Afterwards he gave the god a gift, a white horse.

pie: h₁yód h₁ógʷʰis mért srówōs péruns ní tékʷont. pl̥th₂enóns h₂éǵrons pl̥nh₁ént gʰréh₁mn̥-kʷe ǵʰelh₃wóm bʰúHt. gʷówes gʷowsth₂óybʰos ml̥h₃ént wédos-kʷe píph₃ont. poh₂iménes méwdont téḱneh₂-kʷe wédni lóyget. gʷénh₂es srówom ní h₁yént gʷéHyont-kʷe. h₁ésyo néḱu krépos gʰr̥h₁méni légʰet h₂éweyes-kʷe h₁ésyo mḗms h₁édn̥t.
english: When the serpent had died, the currents ran down from the mountain. They filled the wide fields, and the grass grew green. The cows came forth from the stalls and drank the water. The shepherds were glad, and the children played in the water. The women went down to the stream and sang. But its dead body lay on the grass, and the birds ate its flesh.

pie: deywós h₂éyeri h₁éǵʰs gʷéh₂t. h₁ógʷʰim bʰr̥ǵʰénti péruni widét. h₁ím gʷʰént h₁ím h₂ḱm̥néh₁ gʷélh₁t. h₁rudʰróm h₁ésyo h₁ésh₂r̥ soksóybʰos ní tékʷet. wédōr luh₁éto dʰéǵʰōm-kʷe h₁íh₂ péh₃t. méǵh₂ ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom ḱléwos deywóm gʷémt. h₂yuHn̥ḱṓs h₁ím dh₂pnóy séngʷʰont ǵérh₂ontes-kʷe ḱl̥nwént.
english: The god went out early. He found the serpent on the high mountain. He slew it; he struck it with the stone. The red blood of the serpent ran down from the rocks. The waters were loosed, and the earth drank them. Great fame came to the god, imperishable fame. The young men sang of it at the feast, and the old men listened.

pie: dʰugh₂tḗr méh₂term̥ wékʷsperoy prḗḱst nu kúdʰe h₁ógʷʰis ḱéyor. sokʷéyet bʰágos h₁ím sh₂imń̥bʰis mréy Hn̥dʰí bʰéndʰet. h₂ew gʷémeti. h₁yód gʷémeti h₁ím h₂ew téwketi. bʰéwdʰeti h₂lékseti-kʷe nos. mē troméyes ssdʰí. dʰugh₂tḗr h₂énh₁mom ḱléwt. h₂stéres démi upér luként. dʰugh₂tḗr légʰt swépt-kʷe.
english: At evening a daughter asked her mother: "Where does the serpent lie now?" She said: "The god bound it with ropes beneath the sea." "Will it come back?" "If it comes, he will strike it again. He is awake, and he protects us. Do not be afraid; rest!" The daughter heard the wind. Above the house the stars shone. The daughter lay down and slept.

pie: pérkʷune te ḱúh₁re déywe gʷr̥nHmés. dusménesm̥-ge h₁ógʷʰim péruni gʷʰéns. h₁yós h₂ékʷās spérs n̥smé gʷm̥dʰí. h₁yós soksóm bʰéyds téwe nos wéyHm̥ dh₃dʰí. ḱléwos toy h₂nr̥sú ń̥dʰgʷʰitom. nu toy sóǵʰos h₂r̥Hmós lewkóm-kʷe toy h₃ókʷ. h₁erkʷóm nos ḱludʰí n̥sméy-kʷe priHós h₁sdʰí.
english: Perkwunos, strong god, we praise you. You indeed slew the ill-minded serpent on the mountain. You who freed the waters, come to us! You who split the rock, give us your strength! Your fame among men is imperishable. Now mighty is your arm, and bright your eye. Hear our hymn, and be dear to us!

pie: dusménēs mréy légʰet h₁ésyo-kʷe wédos péh₂st. h₁ím kʷis ne dʰégʷʰh₂t. nu h₁n̥gʷnís ish₁rṓy dʰh₁séy mléwHt wédos h₂sowséyōh₂. h₁n̥gʷnís dʰégʷʰet móri-kʷe yéset. dusménēs h₁ésmōd h₁éǵʰs úd h₁nédʰt. ish₁rós swóh₁ h₂ḱm̥néh₁ sth₂éh₁yet. h₁ím gʷélh₁t só-kʷe néḱus séngʷt. h₁n̥gʷnís h₁ésyo krépos dʰégʷʰet. h₁n̥gʷnís ish₁rós-kʷe ḱóm méwdetām. tewh₂téh₂ dwóh₁ tóh₁ séngʷʰeti.
english: The ill-minded one lay in a sea and guarded its water. No one came near it. Then Fire said to the strong god: "I shall dry up the water." Fire blazed, and the sea boiled. The ill-minded one came up out of it. The strong one stood with his stone. He hit it, and it fell dead. Fire burned its body. Fire and the strong one rejoiced together. The tribe sings of those two.

pie: póyḱos gʷṓs h₂epó h₂éǵet h₁íns-kʷe péruni wérǵt. gʷoldʰóh₁ h₁ésmi h₁n̥dóm HrudHént. bʰágos h₁éysōm wókʷn̥s ḱléwt. só h₁n̥gʷnís-kʷe ḱóm h₂én gʷh₂tā́m. h₁n̥gʷnís póyḱom h₁éwset ish₁rós-kʷe h₁íd swóh₁ h₂ḱm̥néh₁ skélHt. póyḱos bʰéwgt h₁n̥gʷnís h₁ím h₁r̥h₁pyét. léwkm̥ úd h₁n̥dʰént. poh₂iménes h₁íns h₂ml̥ǵént h₂mélǵos-kʷe sweh₂dú h₁ést.
english: An enemy drove the cows away and shut them up in a rock. Inside it they cried out with hunger. The god heard their voices. He and Fire went there together. Fire burned the enemy, and the strong one split the rock open with his stone. The enemy fled, but Fire seized him. They came out into the light. The shepherds milked them, and the milk was sweet.

pie: téḱnom h₂éwh₂om prḗḱst. kʷós h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰént. ǵérh₂onts sékʷt. gʰrómosyo dʰéh₁s tewh₂sós h₁ím gʷʰént. h₁ím h₂ḱm̥néh₁ diwés gʷélh₁t. kʷíd h₁ím gʷélh₁t. wédōr Hwért h₂néres-kʷe tr̥syónt. h₁ésyo dénḱtreh₂ dl̥h₁gʰéh₂ h₁ést h₁ésyo-kʷe h₃ókʷih₁ h₁rudʰróyh₁ h₁stā́m. nu wédōr sréweti píph₃omes-kʷe. téḱnom smḗyt dṓm-kʷe drémt.
english: A child asked its grandfather: "Who slew the serpent?" The old man said: "The god of thunder slew it, the strong one. He hit it with a stone from the sky." "Why did he hit it?" "It had shut in the waters, and men were thirsty. Its fangs were long, and its eyes were red. Now the waters flow, and we drink." The child laughed and ran home.

pie: h₂éngʷʰis dʰubʰróy h₂ewlóy dʰǵʰémi Hn̥dʰí ḱéyo. léwks h₂én ne h₁ést. déh₂n̥wōm srówons h₃dn̥tsú dʰoréyet. deywóḱlewēs h₂ewlóm h₁n̥dó ní h₁éyt. péh₂wr̥ swóy ǵʰóstoy bʰéret. péh₂wr̥ kʷéḱt bʰéyh₂t-kʷe. srówons léh₁t bʰéwgt-kʷe. wiHrós h₁ím sékʷeto h₁ím-kʷe kr̥snóy wédesi moréyet. pl̥h₁uyéh₂ōm h₂éwyōm h₃ésth₁h₂ h₂ewlóy légʰet. déh₂nuh₂ úd h₂éǵroysu upér sréwet. nu wiHrós sóh₂wl̥ upó h₁ludʰét. h₁ésyo méh₂tēr h₁ím kʷéḱt mówdoh₁-kʷe HréwdHt.
english: A snake lay beneath the earth, in a deep hollow. There was no light there. It held the currents of the rivers in its teeth. Fame-from-the-Gods went down into the hollow. He carried fire in his hand. It saw the fire and was afraid. It let go of the currents and fled. But the hero followed it and killed it in the dark water. In the hollow lay the bones of many sheep. The rivers flowed up over the fields. Then the hero came up into the sun. His mother saw him and cried out with joy.

pie: nu toy wéy gʷénh₂es gʷéHyomes. bʰáge nos h₂éngʷʰim moréyes. téḱneh₂ nos wédos píph₃eti. péḱu nos h₂mélǵos dédeh₃ti. h₂ówis nos h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m dédeh₃ti. nu téwh₂se kéh₂ilos h₁sdʰí. n̥sméy h₁wésus priHós-kʷe h₁syéh₁s.
english: We women now sing to you. God, you slew the snake for us. Our children drink the water. Our livestock gives milk. The sheep gives us wool. Be well now, strong one! May you be good and dear to us!

pie: h₁yód deywós h₁ógʷʰim moréyet h₁léwdʰeyes dh₂pnóm h₂réydʰont. péh₂wr̥ h₂idʰént mḗms kʷéroy pékʷont médʰu-kʷe péh₃tleh₂ h₁n̥dó ǵʰwént. h₂yuHn̥ḱṓs h₂néres ǵʰwērés h₁erkʷóm séngʷʰont. deywós gʷémt dh₂pnóy-kʷe sédt. ǵérh₂ontes spéleh₂ sokʷéyont. médʰu péh₃t méwdt-kʷe. h₁éymos déh₃reh₂ gʷṓs h₂ówins-kʷe déh₃t. h₂roh₁dʰéyont h₁uséwōm déh₃tor n̥sméy priHós h₁sdʰí.
english: When the god had slain the serpent, the people prepared a feast. They kindled a fire, cooked meat in a cauldron, and poured mead into cups. The young men sang a hymn about the beast. The god came and sat down at the feast. The old men told stories. He drank the mead and was glad. He gave them gifts: cattle and sheep. They said: "Giver of good things, be dear to us!"

pie: "kʷíd wēlh₁si?"
english: "What do you want?"

pie: deywṓs ḱóm sdént. h₁óynos h₂éǵt kʷós h₁ógʷʰim moréyēti. ne kʷis wéwket h₁éysōm ḱérdh₂ h₂énǵʰesh₁ trémt. nu pérkʷunos stéh₂t wéwket-kʷe h₁éyoh₂. swóns HeHḱúns h₁éḱwons yéwgt. deywṓs h₁ím wl̥h₁ént h₁ésmey-kʷe h₂éḱmonm̥ dh₃ént. ph₂tḗr dyḗws h₂éǵt súHnew moy h₁idʰí pr̥dʰí-kʷe. h₁éyt h₁ím-kʷe pért mért-kʷe. nu h₁ím sepelyónt.
english: The gods sat together. One said: "Who will slay the serpent?" No one answered; their hearts trembled with fear. Then Perkwunos stood up and said: "I shall go." He yoked his swift horses. The gods chose him and gave him the stone. Father Sky said: "Go, my son, and strike!" He went and struck it, and it died. Then they honored him.

pie: dusménēs póyḱos dʰǵʰémi Hn̥dʰér gʷíh₃wet. h₁nédʰt srówons-kʷe gʷérh₃t. h₂éǵrōs tr̥sént h₂óweyes-kʷe tr̥syónt. gʷénh₂es kénkont ǵérh₂ontes-kʷe ḱéh₂desi l̥gʰént. tewh₂téh₂ deywóns HréwdHt. bʰágos h₁ésyeh₂s wókʷm̥ ḱléwt. HeHḱúns h₁éḱwons yéwgt h₁íns póyḱom h₂éǵet. h₁ésyo krépos h₂ḱm̥néh₁ bʰinédt srówōs-kʷe h₁ésmōd h₁éǵʰs sréwont. nu h₂óweyes píph₃ont tewh₂téh₂-kʷe méwdet.
english: An ill-minded enemy lived under the earth. It came forth and swallowed the currents. The fields dried up, and the sheep were thirsty. The women were hungry, and the old men lay down in grief. The tribe cried out to the gods. The god heard its voice. He yoked swift horses and drove them to the enemy. With the stone he split its body, and the currents flowed out of it. Then the sheep drank, and the tribe rejoiced.

pie: h₂nr̥ménēs póyḱom próti h₁éyt. h₁ím ǵʰoysóh₁ pért ne-kʷe mért. h₁ím dwís pért gʰrémet-kʷe. h₁ím trís pért h₁ésyo-kʷe ḱérh₂sō bʰindtó. h₁ésyo h₁ésh₂r̥ kr̥snóm h₁ést. h₁ésh₂r̥ h₁ésmōd h₁éǵʰs tékʷet wédesh₂-kʷe h₁sh₂énh₁ ḱóm tékʷet. srówōs ḱórkās léwh₃ont dóruh₂-kʷe píph₃et. h₂nr̥ménēs stéh₂t swóm-kʷe ǵʰoysóm tl̥néh₂t. tewh₂téh₂ h₁ím kʷéḱt ḱlutóybʰos-kʷe h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥ gʷr̥néHt.
english: Man-Minded went against the enemy. He struck it once with a spear, and it did not die. He struck it twice, and it roared. He struck it three times, and its head split. Its blood was black. Blood ran out of it, and with the blood the waters ran. The streams washed the pebbles, and the trees drank. Man-Minded stood up and lifted his spear. The tribe saw him and praised his famous name.

pie: h₂éwsōs-ge diwés dʰugh₂tḗr gʷegʷóme. h₁léwdʰerons srówons h₂éǵrons-kʷe spéḱyeti. nu dusménēs dʰǵʰémi ḱéyor. bʰágom-ge gʷr̥nHté h₁yós h₁ím moréyet. nu ḱuh₁rṓy kéh₂nmn̥ gʷéHyete. nu nos h₂éwsos h₁wésuh₂ bʰére.
english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, has indeed come. She sees the free streams and the fields. Now the ill-minded one lies on the earth. Praise the god indeed, who killed him! Now sing a song to the strong one! Dawn, bring us good things now!

pie: h₁éḱwōs tu weukʷónt, "ḱludʰí, h₂ówei, ḱḗr gʰe Hegʰnutór n̥sméi widn̥tbʰ(y)ós. Hnḗr, pótis, h₂éwyom r̥ wl̥h₂néHm sebʰi kʷr̥néuti nu gʷʰérmom wéstrom néǵʰi h₂éwyom wl̥h₂néH h₁ésti."
english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

pie: h₁eǵóh₂ poh₂imḗn dʰéh₁sm̥-kʷe sepelyóh₂. h₂óweyes déh₂nus píph₃onti. h₂éngʷʰis-ge déh₂nu dʰoréyet dʰéh₁s h₁íd sélǵt. nu moy téwh₂se h₂ówins wĺ̥kʷōd h₂lékse. nu toy sweh₂dú h₂mélǵos déh₃oh₂.
english: I am a shepherd, and I praise the god. The sheep drink from the river. A snake indeed held the river; the god set it free. Now guard my sheep, strong one, from the wolf! I shall now give you sweet milk.

pie: h₂ówis h₁éḱwōs-kʷe
english: The Sheep and the Horses

pie: pérkʷunoybʰos te ísh₁re ǵʰuHéyomes. dh₂pnóm-ge nos gʷm̥dʰí h₁yós h₁ógʷʰim kélh₂s. sweh₂dú-ge médʰu ph₃dʰí h₁yód toy ǵʰumé. wéyHm̥-ge nos méǵh₂-kʷe ḱléwos dh₃dʰí. póyḱons téwe h₂ḱm̥néh₁ gʷl̥h₁dʰí.
english: Perkwunos, strong one, we call upon you. Come indeed to our feast, you who struck the serpent! Drink indeed the sweet mead that we have poured for you! Give us indeed strength and great fame! Strike the enemies with your stone!

pie: deywṓy néwom h₁erkʷóm gʷéHyoh₂. h₁ógʷʰim-ge h₂ḱm̥néh₁ moréyet. nu dʰǵʰmés h₁ludʰíbʰos wédōr spért. pérkʷune moy kéh₂nmn̥ ḱludʰí. nu nos péḱu HeHḱúns-kʷe h₁éḱwons dh₃dʰí. nu nos dómn̥s nékʷti ph₂sdʰí.
english: I sing a new hymn to the god. He indeed killed the serpent with the stone. Then he freed the waters for the people of the earth. Hear my song, Perkwunos! Give us livestock and swift horses now! Now guard our homes in the night!

pie: ḱuh₁rós deywós ḱuh₁rós-kʷe h₁ésyo h₂r̥Hmós. gʷr̥h₂ús h₁ésyo h₂éḱmō h₂eḱrós-kʷe ǵʰoysós. h₁ésyo-ge h₁éḱwōs HeHḱéwes. nu sweh₂dú médʰu péh₃t Hwérdʰt-kʷe. nu dusménesm̥ ǵʰwḗrm̥ wént. h₁ím kʷis kh₃téwi ne térh₂ut. stuh₂rósyo téwh₂os gʷéHyomes.
english: Strong is the god, and strong is his arm. Heavy is his stone, and sharp the spear. His horses are indeed swift. Then he drank the sweet mead and grew strong. He then overpowered the ill-minded beast. No one overcame him in the fight. We sing the might of the strong one.

pie: h₂éngʷʰis dʰéh₁sm̥ dʰréwgʰt. sh₂wéni légʰet smḗyt-kʷe. sékʷt wédos méǵʰye ne h₁ésti h₂ékʷeh₂es h₂epó lelikʷḗr. deywós h₂epó gʷéh₂t. h₂éǵrōs h₂sowsṓs h₁sént tewh₂téh₂-kʷe HréwdHt. dʰéh₁s dʰrówgʰom kʷéḱt gʰrémet-kʷe. h₂ew gʷémt h₁ím-kʷe gʷr̥h₂úh₁ h₂ḱm̥néh₁ dʰéwgʰt. h₁ésyo h₃ésth₁h₂ Hrunépt wódr̥-kʷe h₁éǵʰs tékʷet. h₁ésyo dʰrówgʰos h₁ím ne spért. h₁ésyo krépos ḱórkeh₂su légʰet tewh₂téh₂-kʷe wódr̥ píph₃et.
english: The snake deceived the god. It lay in the sun and laughed. It said: "I have no water; the waters have gone away." The god went away. But the fields were dry, and the tribe cried out. The god saw the lie and grew angry. He came back and struck it with the heavy stone. He broke its bones, and the water ran out. Its lie did not save it. Its body lay on the pebbles, and the tribe drank the water.

pie: ph₂tḗr dyḗws swṓy suHnówey h₂éḱmonm̥ tḗtḱt. h₂éḱmō gʷr̥h₂ús lewkós-kʷe h₁ést. suHnówey h₁ím déh₃t h₂éǵt-kʷe. ḱóm h₁pdʰí h₁ógʷʰim-kʷe kl̥h₂dʰí. suHnús h₁ím ǵʰóstoy h₁épt bʰérǵʰontm̥-kʷe pérkʷum stéygʰet. h₁ím h₂én póyḱom próti Hyéh₁kt. h₁ésyo ḱérh₂sonm̥ dʰéwgʰt h₁ím-kʷe bʰéydt. nu h₁éy h₂ew deywósyo ǵʰóstom h₁n̥dó gʷéh₂t.
english: Father Sky made a stone for his son. The stone was heavy and bright. He gave it to his son and said: "Take this and strike the serpent!" The son took it in hand and climbed a high oak. From there he threw it at the enemy. It hit its head and split it. Then it went back into the hand of the god.

pie: h₁ógʷʰis h₂ékʷeh₂bʰis péri ḱéyo. deywṓs h₁ím widónt h₁ésmōd-kʷe trésont. dyḗm upó bʰugént n̥bʰróysu-kʷe Hn̥dʰí ḱélonto. gʰrómosyo somHós dʰéh₁s dʰérst. h₁éymos wéwket mē trésete. h₁ógʷʰim moréyōh₂. h₂én h₁r̥sḱét h₁ím-kʷe h₂ḱm̥néh₁ trís kélh₂t. h₁ésyo h₁orséh₂ trémt nu mért. deywṓs h₂ew ní gʷmént n̥ḱéwi-kʷe péri sth₂ént. h₁ím gʷr̥nHént h₁yós dʰérst.
english: The serpent lay around the waters. The gods saw it and trembled before it. They fled up to the sky and hid under the clouds. The god of thunder alone took courage. He said to them: "Do not tremble! I shall kill the serpent." He went there and struck it three times with the stone. Its tail shook, and then it died. The gods came down again and stood around the dead one. They praised him, the one who had dared.
